From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: MerchantSuite - post-demo econ follow-up & next tests

Hi Sanjay — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned.

Key takeaways from the demo
- Primary workload: conversational support (multi-turn, context up to ~1k tokens) and occasional summarization for transcripts. Estimated load: ~80M generation tokens / month; burst to ~400 RPS in peak windows.
- Current comparator: you mentioned your infra experiments with AWS Bedrock + Sagemaker endpoints and Google Vertex AI. Important constraints: low 90s percentile latency target (~250ms), and strict data retention rules for PII.

High-level economics (initial ballpark, benchmarking assumptions below)
- AWS Bedrock (customer quote + published rates): ~ $26 / 1M generation tokens (baseline, no committed discount).
- Google Vertex: ~ $21 / 1M tokens for comparable model family.
- Redwood hosted (typical for this workload, pre-commit): ~ $14 / 1M tokens.
Notes: those Redwood numbers assume an average batching profile and a live prefix/KV cache hit of ~35%. With a 50% cache hit and batch tuning we project effective unit cost closer to $9–10 / 1M (this is what the benchmarking aims to validate).

Proposed tests (what we want to run next)
1) Synthetic 1M-token generation run (single model, controlled prompt lengths) — measures raw per-token time and cost. (Redwood run)
2) Replay of a 24-hour production sample (you provide anonymized logs) with cache enabled to estimate realistic cache hit rates and batching gains. (joint)
3) Burst saturation test at 500 RPS for 10 minutes — measure p95/p99 and graceful fallback behavior. (Redwood run on dedicated test cluster)
4) Billing sensitivity: run replay with two quantization/throughput profiles (float16 vs int8-quantized variant) to map latency vs cost.

Deliverables and owners
- Redwood: bench plan + quick TCO sheet (attached) — owner: Ben (I put the spreadsheet in the Drive link below). ETA: 4 business days.
- MerchantSuite: anonymized request logs or sample sessions (procurement can scrub PII) — owner: Sanjay.
- Both: choose a 2-hour window for the joint replay (we prefer Friday mornings PST).

Ask: can you confirm you can share a 24-hour sample (or a 10k-session sample) by EOD Monday 9/13? If not, we’ll start with synthetic runs and tune once we have data.

Attachments: redwood-hyperscaler-econ-quicksheet-20260909.xlsx (pricing scenarios + assumed cache/batching), MA-terms-draft-Redwood-20260909.pdf (starter commercial language).

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-min bench kickoff once we have the sample logs.

—
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — good summary. A few clarifications and asks from our side:

1) Can you confirm the $14 / 1M number is for generation only (not embeddings)? We did see varying price points across providers.
2) Procurement wants two committed-pricing scenarios: a 12-month 1.5x commit and a 24-month 2x commit. Would be helpful if you can show committed unit price deltas.
3) Important: our security team requires SOC 2 Type II report and a runbook for data deletion — is that in your pack?

We should be able to share a 10k-session anonymized sample by EOD Monday (we’ll scrub PII and token IDs). Also copied procurement to coordinate NDAs and any data transfer agreements.

Can you also include an estimate that assumes a 50% cache hit and a 60% batching efficiency (we want a conservative baseline)?

Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform
MerchantSuite

Hi Sanjay — quick answers + updated economics in the attached sheet.

- $14 / 1M was generation-only, for the model family we demoed. Embeddings are quoted separately (see sheet).
- Attached spreadsheet (redwood-hyperscaler-econ-quicksheet-20260909.xlsx) now includes committed-discount scenarios:
  * No commit: $14 / 1M (baseline)
  * 12mo 1.5x commit: $11 / 1M effective
  * 24mo 2x commit: $8.5 / 1M effective

Benchmarking assumptions used in the sheet (short):
- Cache hit rates simulated at 0%, 35%, and 50%.
- Batching efficiency modeled as the % reduction in per-token compute from request coalescing (we used 40% and 60% scenarios).
- We included a conservative network/overhead add of ~8% to the per-token cost to reflect streaming and metadata overhead.

If you assume 50% cache hit and 60% batching efficiency, sheet shows an effective blended rate of about $6.8 / 1M (24mo commit) and $10.2 / 1M (no commit).

SOC 2: we can share our Type II report under NDA. I’ve attached a starter MA-terms-draft-Redwood-20260909.pdf; legal is on standby for procurement redlines.

Proposed bench dates: Fri 9/17 or Mon 9/20 AM PST — we can reserve a dedicated test pool for the joint replay. Please confirm which works.

Ben
